seal.statement: The 2026-09-18 static reproduction of the critical-spread overflow disagreement produced the learner's refusal only from a synthetic input the live logs do not show, so it is a candidate mechanism, not an explanation. This quest replaces the snapshot with a replay. A scenario is a committed fixture extracted from one live run's artifacts: the priority-partition operations the seed's coordinator created and completed, in their live order with their live targets and outcomes, the membership publication, and the node readiness transitions, every entry citing its run id, node and log time. The replay drives that sequence through the real coordinator and planner on the simulator's seed host, delivers the rows the coordinator wrote to the other hosts' caches in the order it wrote them, and at each live promotion attempt runs a real learner PartitionService count check on the live target node. It sets no state the scenario does not cite: no hand-written node status, planning answer, summary or budget. Done when the seed's real planner, from replayed state, retains the spread-cure ADD at four voters on two nodes as live did; the 2026-09-15 scenario grants every promotion live granted; and, for a failing run whose artifacts carry the guard-input records that learner-promotion-guard-inputs-observed adds, the replay's guard inputs at the refused check equal the live ones on every decisive field and the refusal follows. If the honest replay grants where live refused, the result is a finding that names the first live input the hosts lack; nothing is tuned to emit the label.

text:
Replaced the 2026-09-18 static snapshot with a cited replay (test-only; nothing under src/ changed).

Extractor: test/simulation/critical-spread-scenario-extraction.js turns one live run's artifact directory into a scenario fixture (schema critical-spread-scenario/1) under test/simulation/calibration/critical-spread-scenarios/. Committed: 35052200699 (2026-09-16 FAIL) and 34925405521 (2026-09-15 PASS). Sections: nodes, nodeCapacities (each node's own "Node storage budget resolved" line), partitions (targetReplicaCount + leaderReplicaId, each from the first live line that states it), initialPlacement (the bootstrap [replica-create] hops before the first priority operation), publication (the seed's convergence trace at epoch 2 with all five published), operations (Creating operation / Handling CREATE|REMOVE_REPLICA / Operation completed|failed, priority partitions only), readinessTransitions, promotionAttempts (with the live guard inputs when the live line carries them), plannerRetentions, seedSpreadObservations. Every entry carries {runId, node, nodeId, logTime, atSeconds}; the validator fails the fixture on any missing citation.

Replay: test/simulation/formation-sim-critical-spread-replay.js hosts the real owners per node (createSimulatedNodeHosts) on the virtual network, seeds only cited rows, starts each node's real heartbeat service, wires immediate in-write-order cross-node cache delivery (writer-owned rows only), then walks the merged event timeline. Operations are created through the seed's real RebalanceCoordinator.createOperation and terminalised through completeOperation/failOperation with the cited outcome; the cited CREATE_REPLICA hop inserts the learner services row and the cited completion promotes or removes it. At every live promotion attempt a real learner PartitionService is built on the live target node (systemTableCache = that node's cache, rebalanceCoordinator = that node's coordinator, metadataPublicationReadinessState = a real LifecycleController fed by that node's getPriorityControlPlaneRecoveryHealthSync(seed)) and its real count check runs. Virtual time is anchored so the scenario's decision point coincides with wall time, because two production readers use the ambient clock.

Harness repairs the replay forced: test/distributed/harness/sql-engine-seam.js now parses INSERT OR IGNORE and knows storage_reservations (carried over from the 2026-09-18 prototype), parses multi-line UPDATE/DELETE statements (the owners write them as template literals, so without the dotAll flag every coordinator terminal write silently reported "not a system table"), and honours a trailing "AND <column> IS NULL" first-terminal-wins guard.

Honest result. 09-16: all 122 live count refusals reproduce, with guard inputs identical to live on every field (activeVoterCount 4, learnerCount 1, targetReplicaCount 3, maxAllowedVotersAfterPromotion 4) and completion state converged / planner_ready / temporaryOverflowVoterBudget 0 - from replayed state only, with no synthetic node status, planning answer, summary or budget. 09-15: all 12 promotions the live pass granted are admitted. Receipts: scenario-fixtures-are-cited PASS, pass-scenario-grants-what-live-granted PASS, planner-retains-the-cure-add-from-replayed-state FAIL (recorded finding: the hosts' planner never reaches the retention decision), fail-scenario-refuses-on-the-live-guard-inputs FAIL by construction (no failing run with guard-input records is committed yet; the witness names that exact reason and compares decisive fields once one exists). Probe metric 2, target 0.

The honest replay does NOT grant where live refused: the 09-16 refusal reproduces exactly, from replayed state, with no synthetic input. The receipt that stays red for a reason other than the missing guard-input fixture is the PLANNER one, and the live inputs the hosts lack for it are named here.

What blocks planner-retains-the-cure-add-from-replayed-state. The seed's real UnifiedRebalancer, hosted and leading schema_operations-p1 from the live instant of the first retention (+272.9 s of run 35052200699), reaches the right partition state - "Evaluating rebalancing state {currentReplicaCount: 4, targetReplicaCount: 3}" - but never proposes the count-increasing ADD, so there is nothing for classifyPriorityOverTargetSpreadCureCondition to retain. Two host-composition inputs stop it, in this order:

1. node_endpoints rows. The planner logs "Waiting for transitional cluster membership to settle before planning critical system rebalancing" with blockerReason "endpoint_visibility_incomplete" (10 times). The live nodes registered endpoints: run 35052200699 node-1 at 2026-09-16T03:38:51.769Z logs "Node endpoint registered in cluster" {endpointId: ep-534aa799-...-ws, transportType: ws, address: ws://10.186.0.2:8112}, and the same line appears for the other three joiners. The SEED's own endpoint row is not stated anywhere in its log, so a fixture built only from citations would carry four of five endpoints - and per the projection's rule (a cache holding any canonical websocket row admits only nodes that have their own) that would exclude the seed and make the cohort worse, not better. The artifacts do not record the seed's endpoint row.

2. local query transport readiness. With endpoints absent the seed is the only available node ("availableNodeCount: 1") and the capacity filter then rejects it: "Capacity feasibility filter applied {totalCandidates: 1, feasibleCount: 0, rejectionsByReason: {local_query_transport_not_ready: 1}}". That readiness dimension is not a row in any system table; it is produced by the node's own query-transport wiring, which createSimulatedNodeHosts does not compose. It cannot be cited, and setting it would be inventing readiness.

Both are the same class: the simulator's node hosts are a control-plane composition (cache, CDC, gateway, readiness, publication, storage, coordinator, heartbeat) with no endpoint owner and no local query transport. Until the hosts compose those two, the seed's planner cannot select a spread-cure target, and this receipt cannot be measured. Route: the formation-sim host composition owner (test/simulation/formation-sim-node-hosts.js), not the placement policy.

Second finding, on the PASS/FAIL discrimination this quest exists for. The learner-side budget is decided by the learner node's OWN eligible-node cohort, and the replay makes that visible: requiredDistinctNodeCount is min(3, |eligibleNodeIds|), so a cohort of one turns any spread into "satisfied", zeroes temporaryOverflowVoterBudget and refuses; a cohort of five reports the gap, grants the budget of 2 and admits. Measured both ways in this worktree: with each node's real heartbeat running (every peer's ready lease fresh, as the fixture's five published nodes imply) the check refuses at 09-16 with byte-identical live guard inputs; with peer leases left un-refreshed the SAME check refuses with the SAME guard inputs but through the collapsed-cohort branch instead. The two branches are indistinguishable from the live artifacts, because the live refusal line records only the result. That is exactly the gap learner-promotion-guard-inputs-observed must close, and it is why the fourth receipt cannot be measured before a failing nightly carries those records.

Live evidence for what node-2 could and could not see at the refusal (run 35052200699, all from node-2's own log):
- +296.6 .. +304.8 s, repeatedly, "Partition routing candidates filtered by readiness" for nodes-p1, node_endpoints-p1, services-p1, partitions-p1 and replica_operations-p1: {reasonCode: all_services_filtered_by_readiness, routingReadinessDimension: controlPlaneRecoveryEligible, routableServiceCount: 0}, the seed denied with reasonCodes ["PRIORITY_CONTROL_PLANE_RECOVERY_PENDING", "planning_snapshot_refresh_pending"]. Node-2's authoritative read lane for the system tables was closed for the whole window in which it refused.
- +300.9, +305.9, +310.9 s "convergence decision trace" {decision: skip, reason: not-owner, leadershipTier: tier0-raft-live} - with no publicationEpoch, no coverage and no spread fields, where the seed's trace at the same times carries all of them. The joiner never builds the publication recovery gate the planning answer's summary comes from.
The hosts have neither: the replay delivers every row into every cache unconditionally and runs a full readiness service on every node with no owner gating. Both belong to the same owner as (1) and (2) above.

Third finding, reported not absorbed: the hosts' coordinator runs its real dispatch workflow against nodes that host no ReplicaHandler, so a created operation walks SENDING -> SYNCING -> FAILED on its own 60 s timeout and overwrites the cited terminal outcome's row. The replay passes emitOperationCreated: false so the coordinator persists and admits without starting that dispatch, and the services-row effects it applies are the cited ones; the operation row's terminal status can still end as the coordinator's timeout rather than live's. Divergences are recorded per run in the replay report (28 for 09-16, 24 for 09-15; the REMOVEs are refused by "Priority surplus REMOVE placement fence ... authority_unavailable", which is the same missing-authority class).

Held after probe 2/4 and not continued. The replay reproduced a refusal line, but it also refused four promotions the live run granted, two branches produced the same refusal line, and it needed a virtual-time anchoring seam plus a wider SQL engine seam (INSERT OR IGNORE, storage_reservations, dotAll UPDATE/DELETE). The guard-input logging landed in bb529c57c and nine lab formations then measured the route directly: the closure witness reads an in-flight ADD with a voter-visible target as closure and outranks the derived summary (fourth addendum of 2026-09-19). The node hosts never write replica_operations rows through the ADD workflow, which is the first live interaction they lack for this route; adding it is a broad simulator change the owner declined on 2026-09-19. Nothing of this quest landed; its staged tree is kept at refs/lagrange-scratch/spread-replay-final.
Owner decision 2026-09-19: the broad sequence replay is superseded by a narrow characterization on production owners; simulator quests narrow and never change src.
